deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages). There is an ambient category K and a subcategory M of 'modéré' (tame) objects and morphisms. M contains a terminal object e, a tame interval I_0 and a base point 0: e ↪ I_0. Two axioms from the previous page are used here. Axiom 5° says I_0 is injective in M relative to monos, so tame maps from a subobject to I_0 extend. Axiom 6° says every tame mono Y ↪ X is a zero locus: there is f: X → I_0^n with Y = f^{-1}(0_n), i.e. a cartesian square over e → I_0^n. The previous page reduces the goal as follows. For tame monos X ↪ Y, X ↪ Z, the amalgamated sum Y ⊔_X Z exists in M, with Y, Z → S tame, if and only if there is a tame S' with tame monos Y, Z ↪ S' forming a cartesian square, i.e. Y ∩ Z = X in S'. One then takes S = Y ∪ Z ⊂ S' (sup of subobjects). This page proves that such an S' always exists.

Step 1 (retract case). Suppose X is a retract of both Y and Z in M, with retractions r: Y → X and r': Z → X. Take S' = Y ×_X Z, the fibre product over X via r and r'. Y embeds by y ↦ (y, j r(y)) and Z by z ↦ (i r'(z), z); each is a section of a projection, hence a mono. If (y, j r y) = (i r' z, z), then y = i r'(z) and z = j r(y), so both lie in X and coincide. Hence Y ∩ Z = X, and the square is cartesian.

Step 2 (general case reduced to Step 1).
- By 6°, choose Ψ: Y → I_0^p with X = Ψ^{-1}(0).
- Choose a mono Φ: Y → I_0^n and set φ = Φ|X (a tame embedding into a power of I_0 exists, e.g. by injectivity). This gives a cartesian square X ⊂ Y over I_0^n = e × I_0^n ⊂ I_0^{p+n} via (Ψ, Φ). Do the same for Z with Ψ', Φ', φ'.
- By 5°, extend φ to φ̄: Z → I_0^n and φ' to φ̄': Y → I_0^{n'}.
- Then Y → I^N via (Ψ, Φ, φ̄') and Z → I^{N'} via (Ψ', Φ', φ̄), with N = p+n+n' and N' = p'+n+n'. Both restrict on X to the same mono X → I^ν, ν = n+n' (up to the evident reordering of coordinates), and both squares over e × I^ν ⊂ I^N, I^{N'} are cartesian.
- I^ν is a retract of I^N and of I^{N'} (by projection). So Step 1 gives S'' = I^N ×_{I^ν} I^{N'}, in which I^N ∩ I^{N'} = I^ν.
- Composing Y ↪ I^N ↪ S'' and Z ↪ I^{N'} ↪ S'': a common point has image in I^ν. Its preimage in Y (resp. Z) is X, by cartesianness, and X → I^ν is mono. So Y ∩ Z = X in S''.

This gives the required cartesian diagram (D), and hence the existence of tame amalgamated sums along monos. The purpose is part of an axiomatic, category-theoretic foundation for 'topologie modérée'. The next page re-encodes these data as families of tame functions F_n ⊂ Hom(I^n, I), close in spirit to o-minimal structures.
errors: Steps are compressed (written 'OK'), but the argument appears correct, given that M has finite products and fibre products over retracts and that sections are monos.
The existence of a mono Φ: Y → I_0^n is used without justification on this page. It presumably follows from 6° applied to a diagonal or graph, or is an implicit axiom.

The transcription's 'contractile' looks like a misreading of 'cartésien'. If 'contractile' were the intended word, the argument would not make sense: the squares used are precisely the cartesian zero-locus squares from 6°.

ideas.what: If X is a retract of Y and Z, the pushout Y ⊔_X Z embeds in the fibre product Y ×_X Z of the retractions, via the two sections.
ideas.modern_name: embedding a pushout along a retract into the fibre product of the retractions

ideas.what: Reducing gluing of tame sets to gluing of cubes I^N along a coordinate subcube, using an injective interval object and the presentation of subobjects as zero loci.
ideas.modern_name: gluing / amalgamation of definable sets along closed definable subsets (definable spaces); definable Tietze extension
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries (Tame topology and o-minimal structures, 1998); Delfs–Knebusch for semialgebraic spaces
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is only programmatically announced in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this axiomatics is unpublished

ideas.what: Axiomatic framework: a category M with an injective interval I_0 whose zero loci classify all monos (axioms 5°, 6°).
ideas.modern_name: axiomatic tame topology; analogue of a subobject classifier via zero sets of functions to an interval
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1980s)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches, in 1974, a purely categorical axiomatization of tame topology. Its core is an injective tame interval I_0 and the axiom that every tame mono is a zero locus of a map to I_0^n. From this he derives the existence of tame amalgamated sums along monos. This categorical route was not pursued in the later o-minimal literature, which works with definable sets in a fixed structure.
missed.quote: on trouve des diagrammes cart ... avec carrés cart, et I^ν rétract de I^N, I^{N'}. Dès lors il y a ⇢ S donnant cartésien. OK
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents a categorical precursor (1974) to o-minimal tame topology and to its gluing results (definable spaces). It is relevant to historians of Esquisse's 'topologie modérée' and to anyone seeking category-theoretic axioms characterizing o-minimal-type categories.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine (if neatly organized) proof step: gluing via the fibre product of retractions and reduction to cubes. Its interest is mainly historical, as part of an unpublished 1974 axiomatic attempt at tame topology predating o-minimality.
transcription_corrections: 'diagramme contractile (n° 60)' should likely read 'diagramme cartésien (cf 6°)', i.e. a reference to axiom 6° of the previous page, not to a page number.
'diagrammes cont' / 'carrés cont' / 'donnant contractilité' should read 'cart' / 'cartésiens' / 'donnant cartésien(ité)'.
In the first lines, 'on plonge Y et Z dans Y ×_X Z qui a deux sections X→Y, X→Z' should be understood as sections Y → Y×_X Z and Z → Y×_X Z of the projections; the struck-out word is 'Y dans'.
'diagramme contractile de mono' should read 'diagramme cartésien de monos'.
